Using \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{18}=10^\circ\), the equation becomes

\[
\frac{\sin(n\theta)\sin((n+1)\theta)}{\sin\theta}=\frac12\tan(4\pi/9)
=\frac12\tan 80^\circ=\frac12\cot 10^\circ=\frac{\cos\theta}{2\sin\theta}.
\]

So

\[
\sin(n\theta)\sin((n+1)\theta)=\frac12\cos\theta.
\]

Product-to-sum:

\[
\frac12[\cos\theta-\cos((2n+1)\theta)]=\frac12\cos\theta
\]

so

\[
\cos((2n+1)\theta)=0.
\]

Thus

\[
(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{18}=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi
\]

which gives

\[
2n+1=9+18k.
\]

The smallest positive \(n\) occurs at \(k=0\):

\[
2n+1=9 \implies n=4.
\]

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
